description: We’re building LunaRelay, a lunar south-pole planner that compares candidate landing sites by Sun and Earth elevation over time: sunlit windows, direct-to-Earth geometric windows, and side-by-side site comparison, all in UTC. Looking for help with lunar terrain data (LOLA), SPICE/Horizons validation, and UI/storytelling.
summary:
LunaRelay is an open-source lunar south-pole site analysis tool that helps mission planners evaluate candidate landing sites by computing Sun and Earth visibility windows using analytic ephemeris algorithms (Meeus).

Given a set of candidate lunar south-pole sites and a time range, LunaRelay calculates: solar elevation over time (for solar power availability), direct-to-Earth geometric visibility windows (for communication link planning), combined Sun+Earth windows, relative insolation proxy, and longest continuous Earth-link duration.

Results are presented as a side-by-side comparison table and per-site elevation charts with shaded visibility windows, exportable as a Markdown report.

The tool is built entirely with Python (stdlib + numpy) and vanilla JavaScript — no external dependencies or APIs required. It runs locally or deploys to Cloud Run in one command. LunaRelay makes quantitative site comparison accessible to students, researchers, and early-mission planners without requiring JPL SPICE or Horizons access, while being fully honest about its flat-horizon, analytic assumptions.
details:
LunaRelay addresses the NASA Space Apps "Lunar Landing Site Navigator" challenge by providing a quantitative, honest, open-source tool for comparing candidate lunar south-pole landing sites along two critical dimensions: solar power availability and direct-to-Earth communication link geometry.

HOW IT WORKS:

- Input: a list of candidate sites (latitude, longitude), a start date, duration (hours), and a horizon mask angle (degrees, as a stand-in for terrain blockage).

- Engine: analytic ephemeris based on Jean Meeus "Astronomical Algorithms" — computes Sun and Earth elevation at each site for every time step (default: 60-minute steps).

- Output: Sun-up hours & fraction, Earth-up hours & fraction, combined both-up hours, relative insolation proxy (mean sin(elevation) while Sun > mask), longest continuous Earth communication window, and elevation-over-time charts.

TOOLS & LANGUAGES:

- Python 3.10+ (stdlib only: http.server, sqlite3, json, hashlib, hmac; + numpy for ephemeris math)

- Vanilla JavaScript (no CDN, no frameworks, CSP-safe)

- Docker / Cloud Run for deployment

- Meeus analytic ephemeris (not JPL SPICE/Horizons)

BENEFITS & IMPACT:

- Runs offline with zero API keys or paid services

- Deployable in one command: `python server.py`

- Honest about limitations: flat horizon, analytic (not terrain-aware), geometry ≠ radio link

- Companion Lunar Relay game (match-3 tower defense) teaches link-window timing in an engaging format

- Useful for students, hackathon participants, and early-stage mission concept studies

CREATIVITY:

LunaRelay combines rigorous analytic computation with an accessible web UI and an educational game (Lunar Relay) that simulates the same link-window timing mechanics in a pixel-art tower-defense format, making the concept of communication windows intuitive and fun.

LIMITATIONS (stated honestly):

- Flat horizon model — permanently shadowed crater-floor sites will appear to have more sunlight than they actually receive

- Earth visibility is line-of-sight geometry only, not a radio link budget

- Not JPL SPICE/Horizons — suitable for concept studies, not precision mission planning
